St. Andrew's CofE (aided) Primary School
Welcome
St. Andrew's is a bustling and happy primary school located in the heart of Hove, right by the sea, serving our community’s children aged 4-11 years old.
Our exceptional teachers and staff nurture and inspire the children to flourish and to enjoy a lifelong love of learning whilst helping them to develop the skills to become valuable members of our wider community.We are a Church of England Primary School with a strong Christian foundation, and a fully inclusive approach. We warmly welcome all children of our local area to join our school family.To find out more about current activities, check out our Instagram account.

PSHE and RSE
PSHE (Personal, Social and Health Education) and RSE (Relationships and Sex Education) are part of the National Curriculum and taught to equip children with lifelong skills that will enable them to flourish personally and socially.
St. Andrew's adopts a well-respected scheme called Jigsaw, which is a mindful teaching and learning programme that includes the statutory RSE (Relationships Education, Sex Education and Health Education) and has a strong focus on emotional and mental health and wellbeing.
Jigsaw believes that PSHE is vital for children’s development and that it is most effective when parents and carers work in partnership with the school.

St. Andrew's CofE (aided) Primary School
St. Andrew's CofE (aided) Primary School
Governors
Fran Beckett OBE - Foundation Governor & Chair
I’m delighted as a local resident to be able to support such an excellent school as St Andrew's. I’ve been a Foundation Governor since Easter 2018. I currently chair the HR Committee, and following a brief spell as Co-Chair became Chair of the Board in January 2020.
My work life has seen me setting up community projects, leading charities, and being on various. Government advisory and steering groups. I currently work as a charity consultant in leadership, governance, and strategy development; chair the Boards of three charities; and serve on the leadership team of One Church, Brighton. And in my spare time I write detective novels!
Matthew Greenall - Associate Member
My work in supporting global AIDS, TB and malaria programmes takes me all over the world, and one of the main principles behind what I do is to make sure communities themselves have a say and play an active role in their services and institutions.
As a governor of St. Andrew’s I aim to make a contribution to my own community. Both of my girls went to St Andrew's.
Reverend Dan Henderson
I'm Dan, the Vicar of St. Andrew's Church, Hove. I'm married to Jo and have three daughters, two of whom are still at St. Andrew's
I can often be found at school drop off and pick up being dragged by a large yellow Labrador.
Sophie Thomas - Headteacher
I feel very lucky and privileged to be the Headteacher of this amazing school. The children, staff and governors are a joy to work with and we have such a supportive parent/carer community. I began my journey here at St. Andrew’s in January 2019 and am into my fifth year here and I love it! I have links with churches in East Sussex where I grew up and attend church where my father is an organist whenever I can.
I have been a Headteacher since 2007 and am also a National Leader of Education (NLE) where I have supported other schools across the south of England in a variety of areas such as leadership support and curriculum development. This work is always so interesting and I have learned so much from working with other leaders in many different contexts.
Jo Beer - Foundation Governor
I am a Foundation Governor at St. Andrew's. I am a senior lecturer in Primary Education and I teach on the English and Professional Studies modules on the BA, PTS, PGCE and Foundation Degree programmes at the University of Chichester
Chris Simmons - Foundation Governor
I have a daughter at St. Andrew's, and am so pleased to be able to contribute in some small way to the life of the school. It's been a joy to watch my daughter grow up at St. Andrew's, being provided with a basis for learning, playing, making friends and music, that will hold her well in life.
I am a church pastor, married to my Siberian wife Natasha I met on a trip to Russia, in the late 1990's. It's exciting to be a foundation governor, and to see the school developing and prospering with its great wealth of talent.
Nicola Ryan - Foundation Governor
Joy Robinson - Local Authority Governor
I have lived in the area for 19 years with a keen interested in community. In May 2023 I was elected as one of the two councillors for Central Hove, the ward where St Andrews is based. Having worked for a Multi Academy Trust for 8 years as Procurement and Estates Manager (with a keen interest on Finance), I thought my skills could be put to good use at St Andrews. I am currently Deputy Chair of Finance and Resources Committee.
Becky Parker - Foundation Governor
Dave Smalley - Parent Governor
I am a Parent Governor at St. Andrew's with one child currently at the school and another soon to follow. I am a senior lecturer in Educational Psychology at the University of Sussex, where I have various teaching leadership roles, including the convenor for MSc Applied Child Psychology. My research expertise includes bullying in schools and peer relations, as well as the social and emotional development of children more broadly, but my passion is for teaching. I thoroughly enjoy working with the superb leadership team and governing body at St. Andrew's School and feel very lucky to be able to contribute to ensuring the well-being and growth of children and staff in the school.
Sandra Obidike - Foundation Governor
I have a personal connection to the school, as my child attended and flourished here, which inspires my dedication to ensuring the same positive experience for every student.
I am an active member of the church and bring that community spirit into my role on the governing body.
I serve on the HR Committee and take a leading role in promoting Diversity, Equality, and Inclusion, helping to foster a welcoming environment where every student and staff member feels valued and respected. I am passionate about ensuring the school remains a place where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.
Martin Sacree - Foundation Governor
I am excited to be joining the Governing body at St Andrews Primary School. I have recently retired as Vice Principal at Shoreham Academy and have 40 years of experience in education. Our three (now grown up) children all attended St Andrews School and we have a close relationship with St Andrews Church where myself and my wife are actively involved. I hope and trust that these experiences and connections will allow me to successfully fulfil the role of Foundation Governor at St Andrews.
Sylvia Ruck - Foundation Governor
I recently moved to Hove and wished to support the community by becoming a Governor at a local school. As I am now a Foundation Governor of St Andrew's School I aim to contribute to the school's ethos of a safe and happy environment as well as enabling pupils’ full access to educational opportunities. I have been a Headteacher in Essex in three schools over a period of 28 years and have worked in Essex Virtual School for 7 years, supporting Children in Care.
Charlotte Bailey - Associate Member
I feel fortunate to be supporting St. Andrew’s on their Teaching & Learning committee, as it is a wonderful school with incredibly dedicated staff and fantastic opportunities for the students, in and out of the classroom.
I bring 20 years of teaching experience, in both the UK and Africa. I currently work at a local secondary school as part of the Senior Leadership Team and as a maths specialist. An important part of my remit involves developing staff and delivering the school’s vision for Teaching & Learning. I am excited to be able to bring my experiences and energy to help support and enhance the growth of St Andrew's.
Lauren Newton - Co-opted Governor
I am delighted to have been appointed as a governor at St Andrews. I moved to Hove 4 years ago from London and wanted to find a meaningful way to contribute to the community. I have such fond memories of the schools I attended and recognise how they have played a pivotal role in making me who I am today so I jumped at the opportunity to become a governor. I hope to help create a school environment that allows many other children to feel the way I do about the schools I attended.
From a professional standpoint I have spent the last 15 years in Strategy and People Consulting and so hope that my experience in this space will help the school to continue to go from strength to strength with specific support on the HR committee.
Sophie Ryan - Associate Member

I feel extremely lucky to teach Year 6 and lead music at St Andrew's. I play cello in the Big Noise orchestra and am part of the choir team. Before coming into teaching, I worked in the charity sector in various roles, focused on child protection and deinstitutionalisation. I am looking forward to sharing a teacher's perspective with the governing body as well as drawing on my past experiences in the not-for-profit sector.

Maths
Our primary focus is to support our children to become fluent in mathematical understanding from the most basic level so that they can build upon their own understanding.
Maths Overview Statement
At St. Andrew's we follow a maths mastery approach and aim to:
What is teaching for mastery?
Achieving mastery means acquiring a solid enough understanding of the maths that has been taught to enable children to move on to more advanced materials. Mastering maths is where children acquire a deep, long-term, secure and adaptable understanding of the subject.
The phrase ‘teaching for mastery’ describes the elements of classroom practice and school organisation that combine to give children the best chance of mastering maths. As part of our mastery approach to Maths we work with the Sussex Maths Hub.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maths in the Classroom | St. Andrew's CofE (aided) Primary School
pageCache.text:
St. Andrew's CofE (aided) Primary School
St. Andrew's CofE (aided) Primary School
Maths in the Classroom
What does Maths Mastery look like at St. Andrew's?
We learn together....
Where possible, the whole class is taught maths together and moves through topics and concepts at broadly the same pace. We spend more time on key topics and concepts to ensure learning is well developed and deeply embedded before moving on. We challenge children by asking them to explore concepts deeply through verbal reasoning and our 'diving deep' and 'diving deeper' questions.
We believe that the vast majority of children can succeed in learning mathematics in line with national expectations. The learning needs of individuals are addressed through careful scaffolding, questioning and appropriate intervention where necessary, to provide the appropriate support and challenge. Same day intervention is used to support slower graspers and to address misconceptions.
We use representations…
We use the CPA (concrete, pictorial and abstract) approach to support our teaching of maths. The children are given concrete apparatus (things they can touch, hold and manipulate) and visual representations (things they can see) to help them visualise and internalise mathematical concepts. This allows them to access, conceptualise and solve problems. Without the ‘hands on’ and pictorial steps, this can be very hard for children to understand.

The St. Andrew’s Reading Passports have been designed to inspire children to read a range of brilliant literature as they make their way through school. We have taken time to carefully select the texts for each year group to ensure that children encounter both modern and classic texts; a variety of genres and topics; and characters and themes from diverse backgrounds.
To complete their reading passport for the year, children will need to read at least 6 of their 10 year group texts. Of course, all children learn to read and develop fluency at different rates, and some children might find their year group’s texts too challenging. However, the books can be read aloud by parents and carers, or listened to by audiobook.
When a book has been completed, children answer questions or talk prompts and bring the passport into school for a signature. When they have 6 signatures, they will earn their passport ‘stamp’ for the year.
The school has copies of each text which children can sign out from the school library. However, the year group books can also be borrowed from libraries or bought online or in bookstores. If parents / carers do purchase any of the books and would like to donate them after children have finished we would be very grateful.

Music
At St. Andrew’s, we inspire a love of learning through music and are proud of our outstanding music curriculum and extracurricular activities. Music enhances all aspects of learning and personal growth and we hope to provide the foundations for a lifelong love of music.We strive to enrich our children’s lives through music including a weekly song assembly, classroom music lessons and opportunities for every child to learn how to play a range of musical instruments including the recorder, xylophone, percussion and the ukelele.Further opportunities are available for the children to learn instruments with a number of specialist teachers visiting each week. We have a wonderful school choir and orchestra with opportunities to perform with other schools in the local community.
At our school, music is part of our children’s daily life through:
In addition to school based activities we also endeavour to provide wider performance opportunities with other schools and in the local community.
The Listening Project
At St. Andrew's, we use the Listening Project to help children develop their listening skills and broaden their musical experiences by exposing them to different genres and styles. If you'd like to listen at home, please find the map of pieces here.

Extracurricular Music Lessons
Learning a musical instrument is fun, builds confidence and can open the door to a lifelong passion for music. At St. Andrew’s children are able to take advantage of a wide variety of extracurricular music lessons.
Children who have instrumental lessons have opportunities to perform in assemblies, classes and concerts throughout the year if they wish to, in addition to becoming a member of the St. Andrew’s School Orchestra.
Students can also be entered for graded exams with either the Associated Board of the Royal School of Music , or with the Trinity Guildhall exam board.
If you are interested in your child having instrumental music lessons, please contact our
